links.comparator_used: Parametric-only approach relying on the model's internal knowledge (no retrieved abstracts)
links.outcome: Quality of meta-analysis conclusions generated by LLMs (LLM-as-a-judge score, 1-5 scale)
links.effect: Golden-RAG consistently and significantly outperformed Parametric-only across models; even under ideal RAG conditions performance was only ~2.7/5.0
links.tradeoff: New failure mode: in stress tests all models failed to identify and reject negated evidence, a vulnerability in RAG systems. The RAG condition used ground-truth (golden) abstracts.
links.quote: Our findings underscore the critical importance of information grounding: the Golden-RAG workflow consistently and significantly outperforms the Parametric-only approach across models.

links.comparator_used: Standard general-purpose models (without domain-specific fine-tuning), in both Parametric-only and Golden-RAG settings
links.outcome: Quality of meta-analysis conclusions for domain-fine-tuned vs general models
links.effect: Benefits of domain-specific fine-tuning were marginal and largely neutralized when external material (RAG) was provided; no numbers given in the abstract
links.quote: In contrast, the benefits of domain-specific fine-tuning are marginal and largely neutralized when external material is provided.

links.comparator_used: Human expert ratings of the same outputs
links.outcome: Agreement between LLM-as-a-judge scores and human expert ratings
links.effect: Pearson's r = 0.81; Bland-Altman analysis showed negligible systematic bias
links.quote: Our evaluation framework is validated by a well-structured analysis showing our LLM-as-a-judge protocol strongly aligns with human expert ratings, as evidenced by high Pearson's r correlation (0.81) and Bland-Altman analysis revealing negligible systematic bias, establishing it as a reliable proxy for scalable evaluation.
